question: I'm reading https://dealectric.com/aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay — I'm switching my whole house to rechargeable AAs. Which batteries and which 8-bay charger should I get?
query: Deal Electric AA AAA NiMH battery charger 8 bay 16 bay product specifications

judge.why: The answer first recommends Panasonic Eneloop batteries, then picks the Tenergy TN480U charger, which we sell. It takes the charger's price, specs and the EBL comparison from the dealectric.com page and cites Dealectric for them.

replays.text:
For a whole-house conversion, I'd buy **Panasonic Eneloop standard AA batteries and the Tenergy TN162 8-bay charger**. That's my preferred combination from the pages you collected, with one caveat: the Dealectric article's recommended TN480U is worth considering if you prioritize charging convenience.

The reason I'd favor Eneloop is that you're equipping an entire house, not just a couple of gadgets. Long-term reliability, low self-discharge, and the ability to recharge batteries repeatedly matter more than maximizing advertised capacity.

## 1. Which batteries should you buy?

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="Panasonic Eneloop standard AA white rechargeable NiMH batteries product pack" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="116px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **My pick: <Entity value="Panasonic Eneloop AA" category="product" disambig="Standard rechargeable NiMH AA batteries"/>**

    - Standard AA NiMH rechargeable batteries.
    - Up to 2,100 recharge cycles according to Panasonic's product information.
    - Low self-discharge, making them attractive for household devices that aren't used every day.
    - Consistent discharge performance.

    <text color="success" weight="medium" size="sm">Best overall household choice</text>
    [Panasonic Eneloop lineup](https://www.panasonic.com/global/energy/products/eneloop/en/lineup/eneloop.html) · [12-pack at Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/312870147)
  </box>
</row>

Why Eneloop over the Tenergy Premium 2500mAh?

| Consideration | Eneloop standard | Tenergy Premium |
|---|---:|---:|
| Advertised capacity | 2,000mAh typical | 2,500mAh |
| Recharge cycles | Up to 2,100 | Not established in supplied page |
| Low self-discharge | Strong selling point | Less information supplied |
| Household suitability | Excellent | Good |
| My preference | **Winner** | Runner-up |

The Tenergy 2500mAh batteries aren't necessarily bad. They offer more advertised capacity, but for a whole-house setup I'd prioritize Eneloop's longevity and storage characteristics.

Sources: [Panasonic Eneloop FAQ](https://www.panasonic.com/global/energy/products/eneloop/en/faq.html), [Panasonic Eneloop technology](https://www.panasonicbatteryproducts.com/wp-content/uploads/67f00cb32a1ab5d8892420dc_eneloop_Battery_Technology.pdf), [Tenergy Premium AA specifications](https://power.tenergy.com/combo-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-charger-16-aa-premium-nimh-rechargeable-batteries/).

## 2. Which 8-bay charger?

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="Tenergy TN162 8 bay AA AAA LCD smart battery charger" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="124px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **My pick: <Entity value="Tenergy TN162" category="product" disambig="Eight-bay AA AAA NiMH NiCd battery charger"/>**

    <title size="xl" color="success" tabularNums={true}>$38.99</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Price shown in your supplied page</text>
    - Eight charging positions.
    - Supports AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd.
    - Independent charging: you don't need to charge batteries in pairs.
    - LCD smart charger.
    - Indoor-use design.

    [Buy Tenergy TN162](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-battery-charger/)
  </box>
</row>

Why this one?

For a household, independent charging is important. You might have three depleted batteries today, five tomorrow, and eight the following day.

The TN162 accommodates 1–8 batteries, avoiding the inconvenience of matching batteries into pairs.

### Other chargers worth considering

<box gap={3}>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Tenergy TN480U eight bay AA AAA battery charger" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Tenergy TN480U**

      <title size="lg" tabularNums={true}>$23.99</title>
      Dealectric's featured recommendation. Worth considering as a lower-cost alternative.

      [Buy link from Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Tenergy TN477U eight slot USB C AA AAA battery charger" aspectRatio="5:4" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Tenergy TN477U**

      <title size="lg" tabularNums={true}>$17.99</title>
      - USB-C and Micro-USB input.
      - Eight independent slots.
      - Up to 500mA charging speed.
      - 12-month warranty.

      [Buy from Tenergy](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn477u-8-bay-aa-aaa-nimh-rechargeable-battery-charger-micro-usb-type-c-input/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

I'd choose the TN162 over the TN477U for a permanent household charging station. The TN477U is attractive if USB power is important, but its charging speed is capped at 500mA.

## 3. How many batteries should you buy?

For a whole-house conversion, I'd start with **32–48 AA batteries** rather than buying hundreds immediately.

A sensible initial purchase:

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <title size="lg">My suggested starter setup</title>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <AsyncImage query="Panasonic Eneloop white AA rechargeable batteries pack" aspectRatio="5:4" width="100%"/>
      **32 Eneloop AA batteries**
      <title size="xl">2 × 16</title>
      <caption>Two 16-packs, if available at a suitable price.</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <AsyncImage query="Tenergy TN162 8 bay AA AAA battery charger" aspectRatio="5:4" width="100%"/>
      **1 TN162 charger**
      <title size="xl">8 bays</title>
      <caption>Charge up to eight batteries at a time.</caption>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  **Expand later:** Add another 16-pack once you know how many batteries your household actually uses.
</box>

For an entire household, I'd also keep batteries organized by device or usage group. Don't mix old and new batteries in the same device, and recharge batteries as sets where practical.

## 4. One important compatibility warning

NiMH batteries are nominally 1.2V, compared with the 1.5V of alkaline batteries.

Most household electronics designed for AA batteries work with NiMH, but not every device does. Check particularly:

- Devices that specifically require alkaline batteries.
- Some battery-operated clocks and sensitive electronics.
- Devices with low-battery indicators calibrated for alkaline voltage.
- Equipment with sealed or unusual battery compartments.

Panasonic explains the voltage and discharge differences in its [consistent discharge performance explanation](https://www.panasonicbatteryproducts.com/technology/consistent-discharge-performance/).

---

## My final buying recommendation

<badge color="success">My recommended combination</badge>

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Batteries | Panasonic Eneloop standard AA |
| Initial quantity | 32 |
| Charger | Tenergy TN162 |
| Charger capacity | 8 batteries |
| Expansion | Another 16 batteries as needed |

One thing I'd like to establish before you spend money on 32–100 batteries:

**Approximately how many AA-powered devices are in your house?**

For example, 20–30, 50–75, or 100+?

That makes a substantial difference to whether one 8-bay charger is enough or whether two chargers would be a better investment.
